is_anopheles.evidence: The study focuses on Anopheles funestus s.l. and Anopheles gambiae s.l. (Page 2, Results).

reports_target_markers.evidence: The paper reports genotyping for the GSTe2 L119F marker in An. funestus s.s. (Page 5, Methods; Page 9, Results).

reports_extractable_genotype_data.evidence: The paper provides genotype counts and frequencies for the L119F-GSTe2 marker in Figure 7 (Page 22) and Figure 8 (Page 23), and in the text (e.g., Page 9: '3630 mosquitoes... were genotyped').

african_field_population.evidence: Mosquitoes were collected in the field in Elende and Mibellon, Cameroon (Page 3, Methods).

is_primary_study.evidence: This is an original research article reporting longitudinal entomological surveys and molecular analysis (Page 1).

sub_country_location.evidence: The study specifies locations as Elende (Centre Region) and Mibellon (Adamawa Region), Cameroon (Page 3, Methods).

temporal_resolution_within_3y.evidence: Collections were conducted from December 2019 to November 2020 in Elende and during 2021 in Mibellon (Page 4, Methods).

duplicate_risk.evidence: The study describes new longitudinal collections conducted between 2019 and 2021.

supplement.evidence: The required genotype data is provided in the main figures (Figures 7 and 8).

assessment.summary: This study investigated the impact of the GSTe2 L119F metabolic resistance marker on malaria transmission parameters in Anopheles funestus s.s. populations in two eco-climatic settings in Cameroon (Elende and Mibellon). The study found that the L119F-GSTe2 resistant allele was associated with higher malaria transmission intensity and increased vector competence.
